content:
**Core Fact:** RAG lets you add new files at answer time. You do not need to retrain the model.

# Introduction to RAG

## Introduction to AI Memory and Closed-Book Tests

AI software can think and talk like a person. 
Standard AI models learn from huge data sets during training. 
This phase builds parametric memory. 
Parametric memory means built-in knowledge stored inside neural network weights. 
Weights are math numbers that help the AI choose answers. 

However, this standard AI setup has big limits. 
The AI relies only on its old memory. 
It cannot look at new files. 
When the AI does not know a fact, it guesses. 
This guessing habit is called a hallucination. 
A hallucination is a false answer that sounds very real. 

Training a new AI model takes a long time. 
It also costs a lot of money. 
So, you cannot retrain the model every time a new file appears. 
We need a better way to connect AI to new facts without retraining. 
This fix is called RAG.

## Everyday Analogy: The Open-Book College Test

Imagine you sit in an exam hall in India. 
You face two test styles. 

The first style is a closed test. 
The teacher takes away all books and notes. 
You must answer hard questions from memory alone. 
If you forget a date, you might make up a wrong answer. 
This is like a standard AI model without extra help. 

The second style is an open-book test. 
Your teacher lets you keep books on your desk. 
When a hard question comes up, you open the correct book. 
You read the exact lines. 
Then you write the right answer on your paper. 

RAG works just like an open-book test. 
It gives the AI model access to external files when you ask a question.

## What is RAG? Combining Two Memory Types

RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. 
RAG joins two kinds of memory. 
First is parametric memory. 
This is the built-in skill of the AI. 
Second is non-parametric memory. 
This is an outside database that holds fresh text files. 
Non-parametric memory is a storage box that the AI can search.

At answer time, you can add new files without retraining. 
You just drop new files into the outside database. 
Your AI reads the new files at once. 
This design makes RAG cheap and fast.

RAG also gives source proof. 
Source proof means showing the exact file used to make the answer. 
The AI points to the specific file name. 
This helps users check the truth.

## Worked Example: College Admission Chatbot

Let us look at a clear example. 
Imagine you want to join a college in Delhi. 
About your entrance test, you ask a chatbot. 
The PDF holds exact dates for your test. 

Here is how RAG handles your question step by step.

### Step 1: Chunking Large Source Documents

The college PDF is very long. 
An AI model can only read a small part of text at one time. 
We must break the big file into small pieces. 
This step is called chunking. 
Chunking means splitting a big document into small text paragraphs so the AI can read them. 
Each chunk holds a single topic from the notice.

### Step 2: Embeddings and Dense Passage Retrieval

Computers do not know human words. 
Computers only know numbers. 
We pass each text chunk through a math function. 
This function makes embeddings. 
Embeddings are dense math vectors that show the meaning of text. 
Dense vectors are long lists of math numbers that catch the core idea.

When you type your question, the system turns your question into numbers too. 
This is called dense passage retrieval. 
Dense passage retrieval means turning your text question into numbers so the computer can find matching meanings.

### Step 3: Storing and Searching in a Vector Database

All math embeddings must be stored safely. 
We use a vector database for this task. 
A vector database is a special storage box that organizes embeddings to match text chunks with similar meanings. 
When you ask about the test date, the database does a similarity search. 
A similarity search means finding chunks with matching ideas by checking math numbers. 
The database finds the exact paragraph in the PDF.

### Step 4: Augmenting the Prompt with Retrieved Facts

Now the system gets the matched text chunk. 
It joins this chunk with your question. 
This step is called prompt augmentation. 
Prompt augmentation means adding found facts directly into the message sent to the AI. 
The prompt now looks like this: "Using this text, answer: When is the exam?"

### Step 5: Generation and Hallucination Reduction

The AI reads the prompt. 
It reads your question and the exact text chunk from the PDF. 
Then the AI writes a clear, true answer for you. 
Because the right text is in front of the AI, it does not need to guess. 
This step brings hallucination reduction. 
Hallucination reduction means lowering the chance that the AI will make up false facts by using real source text.

## Limitations and RAG Variants

Even though RAG is strong, it has limits. 
A limit is a weak point that can cause failure. 
The big issue is the retrieval bottleneck. 
The retrieval bottleneck happens when the search system fails to find the correct text chunk. 
If the search system brings the wrong text, the AI cannot give the right answer. 
Also, searching outside databases adds a small computer delay, called latency.

Experts built different ways to make the final reply. 
Two main types are RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token. 

## Summary

- RAG joins the language skills of an AI with an outside search system.
- Standard AI models can hallucinate and invent false facts because of closed memory limits.
- RAG acts like an open-book test by looking up real files before answering.
- New files can be added at answer time without retraining the model.
- The RAG process uses chunking, embeddings, a vector database, prompt updates, and generation.
- RAG reduces false facts and gives source proofs, though search errors can still happen.

## Self-Check Questions

1. What is the main difference between parametric memory and non-parametric memory in an AI system?
2. Why do we need to break large documents into smaller pieces using chunking before doing a search?
3. Does RAG completely stop all AI errors and hallucinations, or does it only reduce them?
